text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Multiple zones reporting p99 tail spikes and streaming stalls for inference-api (route: /v1/stream). Alert threshold crossed at 14:03 UTC, user-facing errors and increased client timeouts. Paging on-call @arjun :rotating_light:

arjun: saw the page, pulling up dashboards. p95 looks okay, p99 for streaming up to 3.8s and some stalls where streams freeze for 8-12s. Egress error rates climbing.

maya: jumping in. Any geo pattern?

arjun: initial graph: eu-west2 and us-west2 more affected. us-east1 minor. Cross-zone ratios spike correlates with NAT conn setup failures and TLS handshake timeouts.

liam: I can run quick NAT <-> gateway checks. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion or conntrack backpressure. Running netstat on one affected node now.

netops-bot: sample from eu-west2-gpu-12: 
```
TCP:  48747 TIME_WAIT  36
no_closed_wait: 0
conntrack-count: 190k (limit 200k)
ephemeral-ports-used: 48900/49152
TLS-handshakes-failed: 0.9% -> 3.4% (5m)
```

jordan: runtime logs show streaming stalls coincide with repeated TLS retransmits on the client flow. Also saw socket rejections in proxy logs (502 during handshake).

maya: immediate mitigation: 1) enable egress-steer to alternate NAT path in affected zones 2) bump conntrack and ephemeral port pool on affected node pool 3) enable short-lived TCP keepalive to flush half-open states. Any objections?

liam: +1 for steering. I'll push a lightweight egress policy to steer pods in eu-west2 to backup NAT-GW-B. Command: 
```
kubectl patch configmap egress-policy -n infra --patch '{"data":{"primary":"nat-gw-a","fallback":"nat-gw-b","steer":"eu-west2"}}'
```

arjun: doing ephemeral tweak on node pool eu-west2-gpu: 
```
echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range_high
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000
```

sara-cs: reporting customer impact: 6 enterprise tenants attempted long-polling API calls, saw increased client disconnects and retries. CS flagged 2 customers with timeouts > 10s. We're drafting a temporary status line to customers.

jordan: rolled runtime fallback to non-streaming short-poll for heavy-tail customers (canary) so they don't hit streaming stalls. Config snippet: 
```
routing: {
  '/v1/stream': { fallback: '/v1/poll?mode=short' }
}
```

maya: after steering and conntrack bump, latency p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.1s in eu-west2 within 4m; streaming stalls reduced but still one outlier pod with repeated TLS handshake fails.

liam: traced that pod's egress path, saw intermittent packet loss on AZB->NAT-B route. Running mtr and tcpdump to confirm.

netops-bot: mtr to nat-gw-b: 
```
HOST: nat-gw-b.eu-west2
Loss%  Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
  0.0%  0.2ms  0.5ms  0.1ms  4.8ms  1.2ms
 12.3%  3.2ms 15.1ms  2.9ms 120.4ms 28.7ms <- intermittent
```

arjun: escalating to infra-networking due to packet loss pattern in single AZ path. @liam, please create a short-lived BGP reroute to avoid NAT-B on AZB while they investigate.

liam: creating reroute now. Patch command: 
```
infractl route apply --zone eu-west2-azb --avoid nat-gw-b --temporary 30m
```

maya: once reroute applied, we saw p99 converge to baseline (~0.6s) and no new streaming stalls for 8m. Marking mitigation success.

arjun: prepping post-incident notes: root cause appears to be partial packet drops on AZB egress path causing TLS retransmit storms that amplify connection setup latency and starve streaming suffix handlers. Contributing factors: conservative conntrack limits and lack of fallback steering.

sara-cs: I've posted a customer update draft to status.redwood: "Interim: We mitigated a cross-zone egress path issue that caused intermittent streaming stalls for some customers. Services restored, we're monitoring. Follow-up with detailed RCA tomorrow."

jordan: action items: 1) increase default conntrack and ephemeral port ranges in node bootstrap 2) add egress-steer auto-fallback policy when TLS handshakes exceed 0.5% 3) improve streaming client backoff to surface early retry vs stall 4) add telemetry for per-AZ TLS retransmit rate.

maya: agree. Adding a canary to run the reroute logic automatically for 5% traffic when p99 > 2s. We'll lift to 20% if stable.

arjun: oncall handoff: @maya taking lead for next 6 hours, I'll update runbook and hand over monitoring. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Monitoring shows sustained return to normal for 20m. Auto-runbook: create postmortem within 24h and link to thread.

maya: logging timeline, will start the postmortem doc and assign owners.

sara-cs: customers notified and support tickets updated.

jordan: uploading runtime logs and tcpdumps to s3://redwood-incident-archives/4463219876/ for postmortem.

arjun: closing handover. leaving note: we should review NAT GW health checks and increase cross-AZ redundancy.

maya: adding follow-up meeting invite for 48h to go over fixes and customer-impact verification.

sara-cs: thumbs up.

(REACTIONS: many :rocket: :thumbsup: on mitigation messages)
